states.basis: Electricians and electrical contractors are licensed professions in Illinois, but the specific licensing statute is not listed among the individual 225 ILCS acts provided. The profession is regulated under Chapter 225 (PROFESSIONS, OCCUPATIONS, AND BUSINESS OPERATIONS), which contains numerous licensing acts, but the particular act governing electricians (likely 225 ILCS 815 or similar) is not shown in the enumerated list and requires expansion of the umbrella container to identify.

Electricians are not listed in the provided chapter titles, but Indiana Title 25 is the state's occupational licensing code. Article 1 (General Provisions) is the umbrella container for Title 25's licensing framework; electrician licensing is almost certainly nested within Title 25 but the specific article is not shown in this list (likely a separate article similar to Article 28.5 for Plumbers).

Electricians are typically licensed under a broad occupational licensing framework. Chapter 74 (State Boards, Commissions and Authorities) likely contains or references the State Board of Technical Professions which oversees electrician licensing in Kansas, but the specific sub-article is not listed in the provided chapters. No dedicated electrician chapter appears in the list.

Electricians are state-licensed in Missouri but not listed as a dedicated chapter like Plumbers (Chapter 341). Chapter 324 'Occupations and Professions General Provisions' is the broad container that typically houses licensing for trades including electricians; the specific electrical contractor/electrician licensing statute is nested within this chapter's articles but not enumerated in the provided list.

Electricians and electrical contractors are not listed in any of the provided Mississippi Title 73 (Professions and Occupations) chapters, which comprehensively enumerate licensed professions. The list includes architects, engineers, and various trades (residential builders, home inspectors) but does not include electricians. Mississippi does not appear to regulate electricians at the state level through these statutes.

Chapter 71 (Public Health and Welfare) is Nebraska's primary occupational licensing chapter that includes electricians and electrical contractors under its licensing framework, similar to how many states consolidate skilled trades licensing in public health or occupational regulation chapters.

Electricians and electrical contractors in New York are licensed under the General Construction (GCN) code, which is a broad umbrella statute covering construction trades licensing; the specific articles governing electrician licensing are not enumerated in the provided chapter list, so the container URL is returned for expansion.

Electricians and electrical contractors are licensed at the state level in Pennsylvania, but the specific licensing chapter is not visible in the provided list of Acts and Titles 1-75. The licensing law is likely contained within a broader occupational or construction-related chapter in the consolidated statutes (such as a 'Professions and Occupations' or 'Construction Industries' chapter) that would require expansion of the consolidated statutes to identify.

Electricians and electrical contractors in Tennessee are licensed under Title 62 (not shown in detail in this list), which contains the state's occupational licensing statutes for construction trades and contractors. The provided chapters are primarily health-related professions (Title 63) and general administrative/municipal codes, none of which cover electrical contracting. Title 62 is the standard location for construction and electrical contractor licensing in Tennessee.

Chapter 101 — Department of Safety and Professional Services — Regulation of Industry, Buildings and Safety is the primary chapter governing electrical contractor licensing in Wisconsin, as it covers building trades and safety regulations including electrical work.
Article 42, 'West Virginia Contractor Licensing Act,' is the specific chapter that licenses electrical contractors and electricians as a classification of contractors under state law.

Wyoming Title 33 chapters listed are profession-specific (Architects, Engineers, Surveyors, etc.) but do not include Electricians or Electrical Contractors. Chapter 1 (Licensing Generally) is administrative. Electrician licensing in Wyoming is regulated at the local/municipal level by individual cities and counties, not at the state level.
